title: Pioneer onboarding: contract staging and SLO readout
summary: Kickoff/readout covering MSA/DPA redlines, SLOs vs SLAs, KMS/egress considerations, pricing sensitivity for pilot, and next steps for legal and pilot. Agreement to send updated SLO table and pricing scenarios; security to review KMS options and request SOC2 attestation detail.
topics: SLO vs SLA and measurement windows
action_items: Maya Chen - Send SLO table with numeric thresholds + two pricing scenarios (hosted vs dedicated) - Due: 2026-03-15
Samir Patel - Prepare short technical appendix on KMS integrations (KMS flow, HSM support, BYOK options) and a one-page runbook for pilot telemetry - Due: 2026-03-16
Asha Nair - Share Pioneer minimum SOC2/ISO evidence list and clarify whether on-prem package will be required for PHI workflows - Due: 2026-03-18
Sofia Diaz - Provide list of DPA redline priorities (data retention, subprocessors, audit rights) - Due: 2026-03-17
next_steps: Redwood to email pricing spreadsheet + SLO table
Security deep-dive scheduled if Pioneer requests on-prem/BYOK
Legal to prioritize three DPA clauses for redline: subprocessors, data locality, audit rights
Pilot start target: 2026-04-06 (subject to contract sign-off)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-11 15:00 UTC | Duration: 63 minutes | Attendees: Maya Chen, Samir Patel, Jared Morales, Asha Nair, Liam O'Connor, Sofia Diaz

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time — Maya from Redwood, AE on the account. Quick roll call?
[00:10] Jared Morales: Jared here, procurement. Good afternoon.
[00:12] Asha Nair: Asha, security.
[00:14] Liam O'Connor: Liam, VP Eng.
[00:16] Sofia Diaz: Sofia, legal.
[00:20] Samir Patel: Samir, solutions engineer, nice to meet you all.
[00:28] Maya Chen: Cool. We put together an agenda — walk through MSA/DPA open items, SLO proposals and how those map to billing/penalties, KMS and keying options, and then pricing/pilot mechanics. We'll leave time for Qs. If anything missing, shout.
[01:05] Jared Morales: That sounds good. Procurement priority is the timeline — we need pilot cost certainty and a clean DPA redline so we can present to Finance by the 20th.
[01:18] Maya Chen: Understood — we'll try to lock on a pricing scenario today.
[01:25] Asha Nair: From security — major concerns are key custody, audit logs and whether Redwood can support customer-managed keys or HSM for PHI. Also need SOC2 detail and encryption at rest specifics.
[01:40] Samir Patel: For KMS we support three patterns: Redwood-managed KMS, customer-managed KMS in cloud (BYOK), and an on-prem HSM gateway for private deployments; each has different egress/latency tradeoffs. I'll outline the flows.
[02:05] Liam O'Connor: Quick question, Samir — if we do BYOK, does Redwood see plaintext at any point?
[02:15] Samir Patel: Good question. With BYOK the model inference path decrypts within a secure enclave on the instance; Redwood doesn't persist plaintext beyond transient memory. That said, we absolutely can provide a security appendix and a diagram.
[02:30] Sofia Diaz: We'll need that diagram for legal and InfoSec. Also, is there a standard clause for key escrows? Our compliance team is picky about escrow for long-term retention.
[02:45] Samir Patel: We have optional escrow integrations but let's table specifics — I'll document options.
[03:00] Maya Chen: Moving to the MSA/DPA: Sofia, I think you circulated a redline earlier — any highlights?
[03:10] Sofia Diaz: Yes. Top priorities: narrower subprocessors list, stricter data retention caps (30–60 days depending on dataset), and audit rights with 30 days notice. Also need clarity on cross-border transfer and data residency for EU-origin records.
[03:28] Jared Morales: On retention, finance is sensitive to longer retention due to storage fees; we want minimum retention by default.
[03:35] Maya Chen: That's fair — we can offer tiered retention: default 30 days on hosted, extended retention as add-on. We'll capture that in pricing.
[03:50] Asha Nair: Also, side note — do you have a point on incident notification windows? Our SLA requires 24-hour initial notification for severity 1.
[04:02] Samir Patel: Our standard is 24 hours for major incidents; we can put that in the SLO table.
[04:10] Maya Chen: Speaking of SLOs, we proposed a set: 99.9% uptime for API, 95th percentile p99 latency < 450ms on short-form generation for hosted, and a different profile for dedicated. Sofia, are contractual penalties acceptable or do you prefer service credits?
[04:28] Sofia Diaz: We prefer service credits as that's typical. Need the exact measurement windows and noise-handling clauses.
[04:35] Samir Patel: We typically measure over monthly windows and exclude scheduled maintenance with notice. We'll send the SLO measurement playbook.
[04:50] Liam O'Connor: From engineering — can you clarify what happens during auto-fallbacks? If the hosted model is saturated and you route to a quantized variant, how do we instrument and detect quality regressions?
[05:05] Samir Patel: We have model-variant routing and automatic quality flags. For pilot we'll expose a canary route and provide outputs for your eval set so you can compare. Also Redwood Optimize suggestions will flag quality drift.
[05:25] Jared Morales: Pricing — we need hosted vs dedicated delta. Our initial use will be a customer service assistant with ~15k monthly messages; can you provide ballpark monthly cost for hosted and for a small dedicated pool?
[05:40] Maya Chen: Yes — two scenarios: hosted pay-as-you-go with token-based pricing and a pilot commitment (30-day minimum), and dedicated reserved capacity with monthly commit and a discount. I'll send a spreadsheet. For 15k messages, ballpark hosted looks like X, dedicated with small reserved pool looks like ~0.7X depending on throughput. We'll quantify.
[06:05] Asha Nair: One pricing flag — egress/bandwidth charges if we route data cross-region — can you clarify?
[06:12] Maya Chen: Egress is typically passed through; if you require EU-residency, we can provision region-specific clusters to avoid cross-border egress fees. There's an add-on for region-isolated instances.
[06:30] Sofia Diaz: And subprocessors — we need a list and prior notification when onboarding new ones.
[06:36] Maya Chen: We'll provide the current subprocessors list and 30-day notice policy for changes.
[06:45] [08:00] (brief side conversation about calendar slots and procurement deadlines, inaudible)
[08:30] Samir Patel: Jumping back to KMS specifics — three flows: 1) Redwood-managed KMS (fastest), 2) Cloud BYOK (AES keys stored in your KMS, Redwood has wrapped keys), 3) On-prem gateway for private clusters (latency implications). For PHI we recommend either BYOK or on-prem.
[09:05] Asha Nair: Do you support HSM-backed keys (FIPS 140-2/3)?
[09:10] Samir Patel: Yes, HSM-backed BYOK is supported for dedicated/private deployments; hosted has a managed KMS option but we can integrate with an HSM for enterprise contracts.
[09:22] Jared Morales: If we pick BYOK, is there pharma regulatory evidence you can provide?
[09:30] Samir Patel: We'll send attestation docs, SOC2 report redacted, and the compliance appendix.
[09:40] Maya Chen: On the contract mechanics we're proposing two lanes: 1) Pilot MSA with a short-term DPA addendum and 2) Enterprise MSA for production. Pilot MSA will cover liability caps aligned to pilot fees. Sofia — is that acceptable to start?
[09:55] Sofia Diaz: That's acceptable as long as the DPA addendum covers the subprocessors and data retention. We'll send our prioritized redlines.
[10:10] Liam O'Connor: Quick tech: do you provide audit logs at token-level or request-level? We need per-request metadata for debugging.
[10:20] Samir Patel: We capture per-request metadata (timestamps, route, model version) and token-level logs can be emitted into your logging sink for dedicated customers. For hosted we provide aggregated logs and can enable more verbose logging as an add-on.
[10:38] Asha Nair: What's the retention on logs? We need logs for 90 days for our incident forensics.
[10:44] Maya Chen: Default retention for logs is 30 days; 90-day retention is an add-on. We'll note that in pricing.
[10:55] Jared Morales: Back to timeline — procurement needs redline and pricing to present on the 20th. Can Redwood commit to sending materials by the 15th?
[11:05] Maya Chen: Yes — we'll consolidate SLO table, pricing spreadsheet, subprocessors, and KMS appendix by the 15th.
[11:12] Sofia Diaz: We'll aim to return prioritized redlines by the 17th.
[11:20] Samir Patel: For pilot instrumentation — we'll set up a shared Prometheus/Datadog dashboard sample and provide example queries.
[11:30] Liam O'Connor: Do you have an onboarding runbook for our SREs?
[11:35] Samir Patel: Yes, a one-page runbook plus a deployment checklist; I'll attach to the follow-up.
[11:44] Maya Chen: Let's talk penalty language for the SLOs — Sofia, service credits are acceptable and we'll propose a tiered credit table tied to monthly availability; we'll also include noise filtration for short GC pauses.
[11:58] Sofia Diaz: Sounds good. Also want an option for escrowed logs if we need forensic evidence for an incident.
[12:05] Samir Patel: We can export audit logs to your S3 with encryption and retention policies; that works well for escrow.
[12:20] Jared Morales: On billing — do you accept PO or do you require upfront card for pilot?
[12:26] Maya Chen: We accept PO for pilot with Net30; for large dedicated commitment we require contract signature and then invoice schedule.
[12:35] Asha Nair: One more on data residency — we will likely route EU patient interactions to EU-only cluster. Can you guarantee region pinning?
[12:45] Samir Patel: Yes, region pinning is supported; there is an add-on to avoid cross-region routing. We'll price that.
[12:58] (brief pause)
[13:05] Maya Chen: Ok to recap: Redwood will send the SLO table, pricing spreadsheet with hosted and dedicated scenarios, subprocessors list, KMS appendix, and a short runbook by 2026-03-15. Pioneer will send prioritized DPA redlines by 2026-03-17 and security evidence/requirements by 2026-03-18. Target pilot start 2026-04-06 pending sign-off. Anything to add?
[13:28] Sofia Diaz: Please add proposed measurement windows for SLOs in the SLO table.
[13:34] Maya Chen: Will do.
[13:37] Jared Morales: Also include an example invoice for pilot month.
[13:40] Maya Chen: Yep — included.
[13:45] Asha Nair: We'll probably request a deeper technical session on KMS in the next week.
[13:50] Samir Patel: Happy to schedule — I'll propose times.
[14:00] Maya Chen: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with email and links to the docs: deck link: https://redwood.example.com/deck/pioneer-onboarding and pricing sheet: https://redwood.example.com/pricing/pioneer-pilot (placeholders).
[14:12] (meeting ends, informal crosstalk)

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker attribution errors possible; some low-volume crosstalk around calendar logistics and finance detail.
